route now copies the Response status and headers and drops the body,

workflow_runs.name: ci
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: handle web Response in auto-exposed HEAD route

head_commit.message:
fix: handle web Response in auto-exposed HEAD route

Fastify auto-exposes a HEAD route for each GET route and supports returning a
web Response from a handler. When a GET handler returned a Response, a HEAD
request to that route crashed with HTTP 500: headRouteOnSendHandler runs in the
onSend phase, before reply.js unwraps the Response, so it received the raw
Response object (which matches neither the node stream nor the web stream
guard) and reached Buffer.byteLength, which throws on a Response.

The HEAD onSend handler now recognises a web Response and mirrors reply.js:
applies the Response status and headers, rejects an already-consumed body with
FST_ERR_REP_RESPONSE_BODY_CONSUMED (same as GET, so HEAD does not silently
succeed where GET fails), otherwise cancels the ReadableStream and sends an
empty body. A HEAD request now behaves like the equivalent GET.

Adds tests: a GET route returning a Response is stripped to an empty body on
HEAD (200, headers preserved, content-length parity with GET), and a consumed
Response body errors on HEAD exactly as on GET.

Signed-off-by: Ujjawal Yadav <81307555+ujjawal-yadav@users.noreply.github.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: feat!: fail closed when a response content type is not declared in the content map

head_commit.message:
feat!: fail closed when a response content type is not declared in the content map

When a route declares a per-media-type (`content`) response schema but the
response `Content-Type` is neither a declared key nor `*/*`, the payload was
previously serialized with a raw `JSON.stringify`. That fallback bypassed the
response schema and could expose fields the schema was meant to strip.

The route response path now fails closed. If the response content type is not
declared and no `*/*` catch-all matches, `getSchemaSerializer` throws
`FST_ERR_MISSING_CONTENTTYPE_SERIALIZATION_FN` and the reply is a `500`,
surfacing the misconfiguration instead of silently returning unsanitized data.

The error handler call path is unchanged: it still resolves the default error
serializer (requesting `failClosed: false`), so error responses are unaffected.

workflow_runs.display_title: test: pin async hook halt behaviour with 2+ async onSend hooks

head_commit.message:
test: pin async hook halt behaviour with 2+ async onSend hooks

Replying from an async `preHandler` halts the hook chain as documented
with zero or one async `onSend` hooks registered, but not with two or
more: the handler runs and overwrites the status code of a reply that
has already been sent, producing a response whose status and body come
from different places.

The existing sibling test registers a single `onSend` hook, so the
boundary is currently uncovered.

Marked `todo` deliberately. The intended semantics are still open in
 #7090 - whether the documented halt is the contract and the hook count
is irrelevant, or whether sending without `return reply` from an async
hook is unsupported. This commit asserts neither; it only stops the
discrepancy from living solely in an issue, so whoever picks it up
starts from a red test instead of re-deriving the conditions.

Suite result is unchanged: fail 0, todo 1.

Refs: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/7090

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: reap keep-alive connections that become idle after close()

head_commit.message:
fix: reap keep-alive connections that become idle after close()

server.close() only reaps the keep-alive connections that are idle when
it is called. A connection that is serving a request at that point
becomes idle once the response is sent, and nothing reaps it, so close()
waits for keepAliveTimeout (72 seconds by default) before resolving.

With forceCloseConnections set to 'idle', call closeIdleConnections()
periodically until server.close() completes, as recommended by Node.js
in test-http-server-close-idle-wait-response.js. The 'false' and 'true'
modes are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Mbabhazi <samuelmbabhazi@gmail.com>

Bump find-my-way to ^9.10.0 and add a `routerOptions.compile` option
(default `false`). When enabled, the router trees are compiled into
generated JavaScript on preReady, once all the routes are registered,

`router.compile()` replaces it on the instance.

head_commit.message:
fix: clamp error statusCode between 400 and 599 with 500 fallback

When an error has statusCode >= 600, setErrorStatusCode passed it directly
to reply.code(statusCode), which throws FST_ERR_BAD_STATUS_CODE. When a
tracing:fastify.request.handler subscriber is active, this resulted in an
unhandled rejection during promise handling. Additionally, setErrorHeaders
did not clamp the upper bound on error.statusCode or error.status.

This commit bounds error status codes between 400 and 599 in both
setErrorStatusCode and setErrorHeaders, falling back to 500.

Fixes #7073

Signed-off-by: Swaraj Jakanoor <169044732+swaraj792725@users.noreply.github.com>

workflow_runs.name: ci
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: key the reply serializer cache by httpStatus and contentType

head_commit.message:
Fix: key the reply serializer cache by httpStatus and contentType

compileSerializationSchema passes httpStatus and contentType to the serializer
compiler, so a serializer compiled for one pair is not interchangeable with
another. The cache was keyed by the schema object alone, so reusing a schema with
different metadata returned the serializer compiled for the first call and the
compiler never saw the new values.

Store the serializers for a schema in a Map keyed by the metadata tuple, and keep
the WeakMap keyed by schema as the outer level. An omitted value is distinguished
from an explicit undefined or null so the key stays stable.

getSerializationFunction is called without metadata by callers that want the
schema's serializer. When only one serializer has been compiled for that schema
there is no ambiguity, so return it; otherwise the caller has to name the pair.

Refs #6987

Signed-off-by: Swarna Sekhar Dhar <bapay.9@gmail.com>

head_commit.message:
fix: key the validation cache by httpPart

compileValidationSchema forwards httpPart to the validation compiler, but
the cache was keyed on the schema object alone, so a second call with the
same schema and a different httpPart returned the validator built for the
first call. validateInput and getValidationFunction read the same cache
and carry the same problem

part gets its own validator while repeated calls with the same part still
hit the cache. getValidationFunction(schema) has no httpPart to look up
with, so it keeps returning the function compiled first for that schema,
which is what it returned before, the docs now say so

the serialization cache got the same treatment in #6990

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(reply): compileSerializationSchema passes null instead of undefined, and ignores metadata in cache key

head_commit.message:
fix(reply): compileSerializationSchema cache key and undefined defaults

Two bugs in compileSerializationSchema:

1. (#6988) Default parameters used `null` for omitted httpStatus and
   contentType. The public TypeScript type (FastifyRouteSchemaDef) marks
   both fields as optional strings, and the docs say the default is
   `undefined`. Custom serializer compilers that distinguish `null` from
   `undefined` (or use nullish coalescing) received the wrong value.
   Fix: change defaults from `null` to `undefined`.

2. (#6987) The WeakMap cache was keyed only by the schema object. Calling
   compileSerializationSchema with the same schema but different httpStatus
   or contentType returned the serializer compiled for the first call.
   Fix: use a two-level cache — WeakMap<schema, Map<"httpStatus:contentType",
   serializeFn>> — so each unique metadata tuple gets its own entry.

Both serializeInput and getSerializationFunction are updated to use the
new cache shape. Regression tests added for both issues.

Fixes #6987
Fixes #6988

Signed-off-by: okxint <cashmein.eth@gmail.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(types): keep FastifyInstance assignable when a custom Logger is used

head_commit.message:
fix(types): keep FastifyInstance assignable when a custom Logger is used

FastifyChildLoggerFactory uses its Logger parameter in both parameter and
return positions, which made FastifyInstance invariant over Logger. An
instance created with a Pino instance (or any custom logger) could no
longer be assigned to FastifyInstance typed with the default
FastifyBaseLogger generic, which is how most plugins and helpers are
typed.

Type the childLoggerFactory property on FastifyInstance and
RouteShorthandOptions against FastifyBaseLogger, matching the
FastifyServerOptions.childLoggerFactory option that already uses the
default generics.

Fixes #4960

workflow_runs.name: ci
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: align request.signal cancellation with the response lifecycle

head_commit.message:
fix: align request.signal cancellation with the response lifecycle

Observe response completion and interruption instead of request close
to determine request.signal cancellation.

Normal request body completion no longer aborts the signal. Response
interruption is recorded before the first signal read, so a later read
returns an aborted signal.

Share cancellation setup across ordinary routes, router error handlers
and the internal 404 fallback. Reuse an existing AbortController when
installing handlerTimeout, preserve the first abort reason, and release
listeners and timers on completion or hijack.

Handle HTTP/2 finish events on interrupted responses and release closed-over
request references before native abort to avoid lazy AbortError stack
retention.

Add regression coverage and update the request.signal documentation.

workflow_runs.name: ci
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: key the validation cache by httpPart

head_commit.message:
fix: key the validation cache by httpPart

compileValidationSchema forwards httpPart to the validation compiler, but
the cache was keyed on the schema object alone, so a second call with the
same schema and a different httpPart returned the validator built for the
first call. validateInput and getValidationFunction read the same cache
and carry the same problem

the WeakMap now holds a per schema cache keyed by the httpPart, so every
part gets its own validator while repeated calls with the same part still
hit the cache. getValidationFunction(schema) has no httpPart to look up
with, so it keeps returning the function compiled first for that schema,
which is what it returned before, the docs now say so

the serialization cache got the same treatment in #6990

Signed-off-by: Abdel <hktitof@gmail.com>

workflow_runs.name: ci
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: run onSend hooks from setNotFoundHandler regardless of dispatch path

head_commit.message:
fix: preserve the caller's own onSend chain alongside the setNotFoundHandler onSend option

The previous commit made onSend fall through to the not-found context's
own chain unconditionally, like preHandler. That silently dropped the
onSend hooks registered on the calling route's own encapsulated scope
(e.g. addHook('onSend', ...) in the plugin the route lives in), which
used to run on a callNotFound() dispatch.

Track the onSend option passed to setNotFoundHandler() separately on
the live context (set synchronously, so it's unaffected by whether the
route or setNotFoundHandler is registered first), and append it to the
calling route's own onSend chain in setContext() instead of replacing
it. Both chains run, and since the option is never derived from
addHook(), there is no risk of running an inherited hook twice.

Also:
- types(instance): add the onSend option to setNotFoundHandler()'s
  options type, with a type test, so TypeScript consumers don't get an
  excess-property error for the now-supported option.
- docs: update Server.md/Reply.md to describe callNotFound()'s hook
  behavior accurately (only preHandler is run explicitly; response
  pipeline hooks including onSend still run) instead of implying onSend
  never applies.
- test: add a regression test covering both onSend sources firing
  together without duplication, and reword a stale "snapshot" comment
  left over from the previous commit.

head_commit.message:
fix: surface the cached lazy build error from every lookup, read the option from the validated config

A terminal build failure cleared both pending builds, so a later lookup that
resolved only one schema kind (the serializer of an error reply for a request
that never reached validation, or the public request/reply lookup helpers)
returned normally instead of reporting the cached error. The cached error is
now thrown before the pending build key is checked.

The option is now assigned from the validated initial config, like
exposeHeadRoutes, so that coercible values ('true', 1) enable lazy
compilation in the route code as they do in initialConfig.

Signed-off-by: Mirko Pira <mp@mirkodev.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: run onSend hooks from setNotFoundHandler regardless of dispatch path

head_commit.message:
fix: run onSend hooks from setNotFoundHandler regardless of dispatch path

setContext() took a detached snapshot of the selected not-found context
and unconditionally overrode its onSend with the calling route's own
onSend. Every other lifecycle hook (preHandler, preValidation, onError,
...) falls through to the live not-found context via the prototype
chain, so an onSend hook passed to setNotFoundHandler() silently never
ran when the handler was reached through reply.callNotFound() (it did
run on a direct 404 hit), unlike preHandler which #6965 already fixed
for the same underlying reason.

Drop the onSend override so it is inherited the same way as the other
hooks, and add regression tests mirroring the existing preHandler ones,
including the registration-order case from GHSA-gm8r-x7h4-fm5r.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(types): preserve `this` binding in RouteShorthandHook

head_commit.message:
fix(types): preserve `this` binding in RouteShorthandHook

Rebuilding the hook signature as `(...args: Parameters<T>) => ...` drops
the original handler's `this` parameter, so route-level hooks like
`onRequest` type `this` as the enclosing options object instead of
`FastifyInstance`. Use `ThisParameterType<T>` to carry it over instead.

Fixes #6974
